title: Choose the new Plexus visual world
question: Choose the system that should govern both the public site and the simpler Admin workspace.

options.label: The Summit Table
options.lineage: multilingual trade-summit agendas, delegate placards, and signed communiqués
options.thesis: Cross-border trade becomes a shared table: every profile, counterpart, decision, and next action has a visible place.
options.viewport: An offset agenda rail introduces the full journey while a large two-party match sequence moves toward a confirmed meeting and the white-label action.
options.risk: Can feel institutional if company profiles and human movement are allowed to become too quiet.

raised.raise: Hierarchy is built from decisive overlapping color fields rather than generic card shadows.
Every workflow keeps its visible trail, so users can understand where they came from and what unlocks next.
One live readiness measure gets physical presence; decorative metric walls do not.

options.label: Trade Mission Briefing Folio
options.lineage: trade-delegation briefing books, tabbed dossiers, and fold-out corridor maps
options.thesis: Plexus is the working brief that turns a delegation’s fragmented records into one accountable route to agreement.
options.viewport: A fold-out corridor map shares the first view with a concise operator brief, a prominent white-label action, and a real profile-to-agreement route.
options.risk: It is the most familiar grounded direction and can feel procedural unless the live route remains dominant.

options.label: The Corridor Tile Hall
options.lineage: azulejo station halls translated into a multilingual exchange journey
options.thesis: The cross-border journey unfolds as cobalt narrative panels whose seams make every stage and handoff honest.
options.viewport: A whole-tile journey from profile to agreement spans the page while the primary action sits inside a restrained cobalt cartouche.
options.case: It matches the corridor story and sequential clarity, but the ornament needs strict restraint inside the Admin workspace.
options.risk: Pattern density can compete with operational data and tenant branding.

options.label: Layered Exchange
options.thesis: Matches and approvals assemble as vivid flat layers that reveal the path beneath.
options.viewport: A symmetrical exchange path assembles outward from two company profiles toward one shared agreement.
options.case: The mechanism translates, but the folk-art identity does not clearly belong to Plexus’s cross-market operator audience.
options.kept: Decisive overlap can create depth without a shadow-heavy card system.
options.risk: Can read as decorative culture sampling rather than credible shared infrastructure.

options.label: Linked Record Stack
options.thesis: Every company, match, meeting, and agreement is an addressable card in one visible trail.
options.viewport: A fixed record stack opens directly on a live match and its back-linked history.
options.case: Its linked-record model is clear, but the retro interface weakens enterprise trust and multilingual expression.
options.kept: The redesigned workspace keeps a visible, recoverable navigation trail.
options.risk: The reference can overpower the product and become nostalgia software.

options.label: Readiness Counter
options.thesis: Operational readiness becomes a bank of physical counts that change only when real workflow state changes.
options.viewport: One readiness count dominates beside the concrete steps required to move it.
options.case: It gives metrics presence, but quantities are not the product’s primary public story.
options.kept: One meaningful live measure may carry more weight than a wall of generic statistics.
options.risk: A dark instrument panel would repeat the current technology-first problem.

options.label: Exchange Session
options.thesis: Each business encounter is presented with the urgency and specificity of a one-time recorded session.
options.viewport: A sharply cropped business encounter meets an oversized one-line offer and a compact route to action.
options.case: It wins attention, but it depends on human imagery not yet held as proof and does not scale cleanly into Admin operations.
options.kept: The chosen direction must match its compositional courage and decisive cropping.
options.risk: Without verified photography it becomes an advertising costume rather than a trustworthy system.

options.label: Hand-Stamped Network
options.thesis: Each cross-border milestone receives a warm, tactile stamp of completion.
options.viewport: A friendly world map links stamped milestones across the full first view.
options.case: The warmth is useful, but the sustainability-coded identity misstates Plexus and reduces operational precision.
options.kept: The new system should retain human material warmth instead of returning to anonymous glass and glow.
options.risk: It signals organic retail and lifestyle branding rather than governed B2B operations.

canonCard.label: Premium B2B SaaS
canonCard.thesis: The expected enterprise landing page and dashboard, executed with excellent hierarchy and product mockups.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional headline-and-product hero leads into proof, features, roles, and a closing conversion block.
canonCard.risk: Highly legible and familiar, but indistinguishable from the category by design.
